Subject: Info request: Japan routing + fallback to SCCs/TIA scope

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal at Kensho asked us to provide explicit mapping of where customer data will be processed for the Japan pilot. Specifically they want:

- A short table showing the primary processing location(s) for inference requests from Japan (edge sites + regional cloud),
- The fallback order if the primary region is unavailable (e.g., EU with SCCs, or US with additional safeguards),
- Any planned use of subprocessors that will access plaintext logs or payloads, and the controls for each.

Can you share the transfer-control matrix and a minimal evidence pack (attestations, retention policy excerpts)? They mentioned SCCs and the UK IDTA as potential cover but want clarity on how we would route and which agreements apply per hop (TIA/DTIA sequencing).

We have a soft deadline for vendor security review on 2026-10-26. Appreciate anything you can share earlier.

Best,
Yuki
Head of IT Compliance — Zenkai Health (Japan)

[attachment: kensho-questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Hi Yuki / Emma —

Thanks — happy to assemble this. Quick summary up front so legal can triage:

- Primary: APAC region (Tokyo) inference fleet — covered by Redwood DPA + local residency controls.
- Fallback: EU (Frankfurt) using standard EU SCCs with our TIA sequencing; next fallback is US-west with documented contractual safeguards and additional access controls (narrowed keys, strict logging).
- Subprocessor note: we use a caching/edge provider in APAC (partner) — they have pseudonymization and restricted KV access. Any subprocessors that can see unredacted payloads are listed and require attested SOC2-type controls.

I have started a control-mapping workbook and a short TIA scope PDF. Attaching the draft files: scc-mapping.xlsx and tia-scope.pdf.

Kimberly — can you confirm whether the planned fallbacks will rely on SCCs only, or if we need a UK IDTA addendum for any UK-hosted hops?

Laura — can you pull the latest evidence index for Kensho (retention policy extract + KMS attestation) and add it to the Drive link below?

I should have the consolidated packet by Wednesday EOD our time (21 Oct).

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachments: scc-mapping.xlsx, tia-scope.pdf]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Info request: Japan routing + fallback to SCCs/TIA scope

Thanks Camila. Short answer: if the fallback target is in the EU we will rely on the EU SCCs (controller-processor addendum) + our TIA sequencing (DTIA when needed). If any processing hops land in the UK, we will require the UK IDTA + our standard UK addendum.

Important clarifications for Kensho:
- SCCs are applicable for EU-bound fallbacks and cover the transfer legal basis for the data at rest / in transit across the boundary, but they do not change operational access controls — we must still document who can access raw payloads in each subprocessor.
- The TIA (technical and organizational mappings) will list which artifacts are evidence (KMS logs, KV access roles, cache TTLs). For Japan pilot, expect a short TIA (2–3 pages) that references the longer DTIA artifact bundle if they request full audit evidence.

I'll draft a two-paragraph explainer on the difference between SCC fallback vs. IDTA applicability and post it to the Drive folder.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
